name: Adjudicate small-ticket credit applications
summary: Applications up to $250,000 are scored by a rule-based decision engine, which approves or declines about a quarter of them automatically and refers the rest to a team of 16 credit analysts. An analyst reads the bureau reports, weighs the business, industry and equipment, checks any existing relationship and either decides within delegated authority, asks the originator for bank statements or financial statements, or passes the recommendation to a senior analyst or the credit manager. Decisions go back to the vendor desk, broker desk or account executive, and appeals come back for another look. Speed matters because dealers and brokers send the same deal to competing lessors, and most delay comes from queues at busy times and waiting for customers' documents.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size privately owned Canadian independent equipment lessor deciding about 3,000 small-ticket applications a month with 16 analysts, 3 senior analysts and a manager.
baseline.notes: Rule-based scorecard and decision engine with an auto-approval matrix for small clean deals; files referred to analysts in a portal queue; laddered delegated authority.

trigger: A set-up application, a fraud-cleared file, an appeal or a decision returned from higher authority enters the small-ticket queue.
end_state: A credit decision (approval, conditional approval or decline) is released to the originating desk, or the file is withdrawn, referred to fraud review or submitted above authority.

volume.seasonality: Follows applications: busier in spring and early autumn and at month ends; about 15% lower in the second quarter of 2020.

evidence.note: From the organisation's process map: about 87% of the 3,430 applications a month are $250,000 or less, plus appeals and returned files.

Duties from a Canadian lessor posting; organisation file cost (Job Bank NOC 11109 wage scaled to 2019-2022, loaded x1.35). About 13 of the 16 analysts' time; the rest goes to lease assumption credit, appeals discussions and file reviews.
Senior analysts spend about half their time reviewing escalated recommendations and sampling decisions, the rest deciding complex files and coaching (tier C share).
The manager approves files above senior authority and handles exceptions; most time goes to staffing, policy and reporting.

systems.name: Vendor and broker application portal with origination workflow and document generation
Rule-based credit scoring and decision engine
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Commercial and consumer credit bureau portals (Equifax, PayNet)
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Used equipment value guides, auction results and dealer listings

steps.name: File arrives in small-ticket credit
steps.description: A file reaches small-ticket credit from intake as a newly set-up application, from the fraud analyst as a cleared file, from the sales desks as an appeal or change request, or back from the director or chief credit officer with a decision on a file sent above authority.

evidence.note: Shares derived from the organisation file's volumes: about 2,690 routed applications, 100 fraud clearances, 180 appeals and 30 returned decisions a month.

steps.name: Decision engine scores the application
steps.description: The rule-based decision engine combines the commercial and personal bureau scores with application data such as time in business, industry, equipment type and amount, applies policy knock-out rules and the auto-approval matrix, and either approves small clean deals, declines on a hard rule or refers the file to an analyst.

error.defect_description: A rule set loaded with a wrong cut-off after a release approves or declines files it should refer.

control.basis: Credit policy scorecard cut-offs and auto-approval matrix approved by the chief credit and risk officer

evidence.note: Scorecard auto-decisioning is documented. A leading US small-ticket lessor auto-decided 41% (2014) and 55% (2019) of applications at an average of $14,000 to $16,000, and automated approvals were capped at $15,000 to $25,000 at another; the 26% used here is a tier C estimate for a Canadian independent with a $36,000 average deal.

steps.name: Analyst opens file from queue
steps.description: A credit analyst takes the next file from the small-ticket queue, with vendor deals flagged as priority, reads the coordinator's set-up summary and the engine's score and reason codes, and checks the requested amount, term and structure.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of small-ticket credit departments; queues build mid-morning and late afternoon, and files arriving after hours wait overnight.

steps.name: Review bureau reports
steps.description: The analyst reads the commercial reports for payment index, delinquency and failure scores, trade lines, collections and legal items and the PayNet lease history, then each guarantor's personal report for score, utilisation, recent inquiries, collections and bankruptcies.

error.defect_description: A derogatory item such as a recent judgment is overlooked.

evidence.note: Report contents and analyst review of owner credit are documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Review business, industry and equipment
steps.description: The analyst weighs time in business, industry risk, how essential the equipment is to the business, its resale market and the dealer's track record, and compares the amount with what a business of this size can carry. Used, specialised or private-sale equipment gets a value check.

next.condition: used or specialised equipment needs a value check
new equipment from a known dealer

evidence.note: Time-in-business rules and analyst judgment on structure are documented; the 20% value-check share is tier C.

steps.name: Check used-equipment value
steps.description: The analyst looks up recent auction results, dealer listings or a value guide for the make, model, year and hours, compares them with the invoice price to spot inflated invoices and decides how much can be advanced against the asset.

error.defect_description: Value overestimated for a niche asset.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of small-ticket credit departments; online auction data were widely used by 2019.

steps.name: Check existing relationship performance
steps.description: For returning customers and guarantors the analyst opens the lease management system to review how past and current contracts have paid, any returned debits, deferrals or collection notes, and the total exposure after this deal.

evidence.note: Analysts request more information when it is insufficient; the 24% share is tier C.

steps.name: Request additional information
steps.description: The analyst posts a request in the portal and emails the originating desk for what is needed to decide: typically three months of business bank statements, financial statements for larger deals, an explanation of a derogatory item, proof of a down payment or a second guarantor.

evidence.note: Requests for more information and bank statements for young businesses are documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Customer provides the information
steps.description: The vendor desk, broker or account executive asks the customer for the documents, and the customer downloads statements from online banking or asks the accountant for financial statements. Some customers do not reply or buy elsewhere.
outputs: bank statements, financial statements or explanation

next.condition: no reply within the hold period

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of small-ticket credit departments; four hours to five days.

steps.name: Analyse additional information
steps.description: The analyst reads the bank statements for average balances, regular deposits, returned items and other lenders' payments, or the financial statements for revenue, profit and debt, and records the figures that support the decision.

error.defect_description: Statement figures misread, for example a transfer counted as revenue.

evidence.note: Financial statement review above a dollar threshold is documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Decide and structure
steps.description: The analyst decides to approve as requested, approve with conditions such as a larger down payment, a security deposit, an extra guarantor or a shorter term, or decline, re-scoring the file when the structure changes. Recommendations above the analyst's authority go to a senior analyst.
inputs: bureau, business, asset and relationship assessments

error.defect_description: Decision outside policy without an exception noted.

control.basis: Delegated credit authority: individual analyst approval limits by amount and risk grade set in credit policy

next.condition: above the analyst's authority or a policy exception

evidence.note: Individual approval limits, structured approvals and approved, conditioned or rejected outcomes are documented; branch shares are tier C.

steps.name: Record decision rationale and conditions
steps.description: The analyst enters the decision, risk grade, conditions and reason codes in the portal and writes a short rationale, logging any policy exception so it can be tracked in portfolio reporting.

error.defect_description: Condition recorded incompletely, so documentation prepares the wrong structure.

control.basis: Credit policy documentation standard and aggregate exception tracking

evidence.note: Documenting decisions and tracking exceptions are documented practice; the approval share is tier C.

steps.name: Senior analyst reviews recommendation
steps.description: A senior analyst reads the analyst's recommendation and the file, questions the structure or conditions, and approves or declines within senior authority, sends the file back for more information, or passes it to the credit manager.

control.basis: Delegated credit authority: second signature above the analyst limit

evidence.note: Laddered authorities are documented; times and shares are tier C.

steps.name: Release approval to originator
steps.description: The portal posts the approval with its conditions, expiry date and approved structure to the originating desk's view and sends the standard approval notice, which starts the sales desk's conversation with the dealer, broker or customer.

next.condition: picked for the senior analyst's sample

evidence.note: Automatic notification of decisions and approvals valid for a set period are documented; the condition share is tier C.

steps.name: Release decline with reasons
steps.description: The portal posts the decline with its reason codes to the originating desk, which tells the dealer, broker or customer and may come back with new information as an appeal.

evidence.note: Automatic decline notices are documented.

steps.name: Credit manager reviews and approves
steps.description: The small-ticket credit manager reviews files above senior authority, larger exposures or policy exceptions, often after a conversation with the senior analyst, and approves, declines or prepares to send the file above authority to the director or chief credit officer.

control.basis: Delegated credit authority: manager approval limit and policy exception approval

evidence.note: Approval authority commensurate with amount and risk is documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Review appeal or change request
steps.description: The analyst who made the decision reads the appeal or change request, such as a larger down payment, a co-signer, a different structure or an explanation of a bureau item, pulls any new report needed and sends the file back to decision.

evidence.note: Analysts work with brokers on structural changes until the deal closes; times are tier C.

steps.name: Record higher-authority decision
steps.description: When the director or chief credit officer returns a decision on a file sent above authority, the analyst enters the decision and any added conditions in the portal so it can be released to the originator.

error.defect_description: An added condition is not transcribed.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of small-ticket credit departments; a short transcription.

steps.name: Senior analyst samples decisions
steps.description: A senior analyst re-reviews a small sample of auto-approvals and analyst approvals each week against policy, checks that exceptions were logged and reports findings to the credit manager for coaching or rule changes.

control.basis: Credit quality assurance: post-decision sample review of auto-decisions and analyst approvals

evidence.note: Exception tracking and credit reviews are documented practice; the 3% sample is tier C.

steps.name: Refer file to fraud analyst
steps.description: When the analyst sees signs of fraud, such as an inflated invoice, a dealer that cannot be verified or documents that look altered, the analyst puts the file on hold and refers it to the fraud analyst with notes.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of small-ticket credit departments; a referral note and hold.

steps.name: Prepare submission above authority
steps.description: A senior analyst writes a short credit submission with the deal, exposure, bureau and cash flow summary, the policy exceptions and the recommended structure, and sends it to the director of credit or the chief credit and risk officer for a decision.

evidence.note: Committee and senior approval for larger amounts is documented; times are tier C.

exceptions.name: Additional information requested
exceptions.description: The analyst needs bank statements, financial statements, an explanation or a second guarantor; the file waits for the customer and about one in five is never completed.

exceptions.name: Escalated above analyst authority
exceptions.description: Larger amounts, weaker grades or policy exceptions need a senior analyst's second signature, and some go on to the credit manager.

exceptions.name: Submitted above small-ticket authority
exceptions.description: Files beyond the manager's limit or with major exceptions are written up for the director or chief credit officer and come back later as returned decisions.

exceptions.name: Appeal or change request
exceptions.description: The dealer or broker comes back with a larger down payment, a co-signer or an explanation and the analyst decides again.

exceptions.name: Used or specialised equipment
exceptions.description: The analyst checks auction results and listings to confirm the invoice price and sets an advance limit.

exceptions.name: Fraud concern found during review
exceptions.description: The analyst finds an inflated invoice, an unverifiable dealer or altered documents and refers the file to the fraud analyst.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from entering small-ticket credit to decision released
benchmarks.population: Small-ticket credit at Canadian independent lessors, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Sources range from two hours (a US leader, deals under $50,000) and two to four business hours to same day and 24 to 48 hours (a Canadian broker network). The p50 of about four hours is the author's choice within that range for a mid-size Canadian independent; the p90 reflects files waiting for documents.

benchmarks.unit: share of new applications decided by scorecard
benchmarks.population: A US small-ticket lessor working through dealers, average deal $14,000 to $16,000

evidence.note: Stated in the 10-K filings. This workflow assumes 26% for this organisation (tier C) because its deals are larger.
Shows automated approvals were confined to the smallest deals in the reference period.

benchmarks.population: 25 large US equipment finance companies, August 2019

evidence.note: Stated in the release. Independents that take shopped deals approve fewer; this workflow uses the organisation file's 66% (tier C).
3,000 applications over about 21 working days for 16 analysts and 3 seniors; Marlin decided far more per analyst with smaller deals and more automation.

pain_points.description: Files queue for hours at busy times and overnight while dealers and brokers shop the same deal to competing lessors, so a slower answer loses business even when the credit is good.

evidence.note: Competitors' two-hour and two-to-four-hour decision times are documented; queue waits are tier C.

pain_points.description: Requests for bank statements or financial statements stall about a fifth of referred files for days, and many customers never send them.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Escalations wait for senior analysts and the manager, who also carry their own files.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: The auto-approval matrix covers only small clean deals, so most files still need an analyst to read reports the engine has already scored.

evidence.note: Low automated approval limits are documented for the period.

sources.title: Marlin Business Services Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2019
sources.supports: About 55% of new applications were auto-decisioned with proprietary scorecards in 2019; within two hours of receipt the analyst is usually ready to decide deals under $50,000; when information is insufficient the analyst requests more; transactions over $150,000 get more scrutiny, which may include financial statements; approvals are typically valid for up to 90 days; average transaction about $16,000.

sources.title: Marlin Business Services Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2014
sources.supports: 17 credit analysts averaging about 12 years of experience; scorecards used on about 41% of credit decisions on new applications in 2014; decisions generally within two hours; transactions over $100,000 receive more scrutiny; about 914,000 applications processed and 383,000 leases originated since 1997.

sources.title: TimePayment raises its automated approval limit to $25K
sources.supports: A US small-ticket lessor raised its limit for automated approvals of qualified lessees from $15,000 to $25,000 in November 2022, letting dealers go straight to documents.

sources.title: Credit Analyst, Bennington Financial (job posting)
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment lessor's credit analyst adjudicates deals of $50,000 to $100,000, recommends acceptance, pricing and structure, creates custom structured approvals within defined guidelines and works with broker partners on each approval until the deal closes.

sources.title: Comptroller's Handbook: Loan Portfolio Management (April 1998, updated June 2017)
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.supports: A loan policy should name who may approve credit and set specific approval limits commensurate with the officer's experience and the type, amount and risk of credit; laddered or joint authorities and committees are used for larger amounts; policy and underwriting exceptions should be tracked in aggregate.

sources.title: ELFA Monthly Leasing and Finance Index, August 2019
sources.supports: Credit approvals totaled 76.6% of decisions submitted in August 2019 at 25 large US equipment finance companies; receivables over 30 days 2.0%.

sources.title: Oracle Financial Services Lending and Leasing: Lease Origination User Guide, Underwriting
sources.supports: After the bureau pull the system assigns a custom credit score and sends the application to auto-approve, auto-reject or the underwriting queue; decisions are approved, conditioned, rejected or withdrawn; changed data requires a re-score.

sources.title: EasyLease: equipment and vendor leasing
sources.supports: Canadian leasing applications have a quick turnaround of 24 to 48 hours; businesses under two years old are limited to $70,000 and need a personal guarantee and net worth statement; from $80,000 two years of financial statements are required.

sources.title: Applying for financing (help centre)
sources.supports: Approval typically notified to the dealer after 2 to 4 business hours.

sources.title: Offer equipment financing to your customers
sources.supports: One application covers $10,000 to $500,000; no financial statements or tax returns up to $250,000; same-day decisions.

sources.title: Equifax Business Credit Report user guide
sources.supports: Payment Index 0 to 99 (closer to zero means creditors paid within terms), Commercial Delinquency Score 101 to 662 and Business Failure Risk Score 1001 to 1722, with trade, collection, legal and inquiry detail.

sources.title: Wages: Finance and credit administrator in Ontario (NOC 11109)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $23.00, median $36.92, high $66.46 (2023-2024).

assumptions: About 26% of new applications are decided by the engine (22% approved, 4% declined). This is well below Marlin's 55% because the average small-ticket deal here is about $36,000 and the range runs to $250,000.
Approval shares are set so that roughly 66% of decided applications are approved, matching the organisation file; about a third of approvals carry conditions or a counter-offer.

Delegated authority is laddered: analysts decide within their limit, senior analysts give a second signature above it, the manager approves larger exposures and exceptions, and files beyond the manager go to the approve-credit-above-authority process. The exact dollar limits are not modelled.
Cases that start from the approve-credit-above-authority process are decisions coming back; recording and releasing them is part of this process.
Triggers from credit policy and system releases change rules and cut-offs; they do not start cases, so their share is 0.
Staffing: about 13 of 16 analysts, 1.6 of 3 senior analysts and 0.3 of the manager's time are on this process.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
